title: Naboth's Vineyard
lead: Naboth of Jezreel refused to sell his family vineyard to King Ahab, was framed by Jezebel with false witnesses and stoned, and became the Bible's classic case of a ruler's injustice against an ordinary landholder.

sections.b: Naboth's refusal rests on the law that family land is the LORD's gift and cannot be sold for good (1 Kings 21:3; Leviticus 25:23). Jezebel uses a fast and two false witnesses to have him killed, and Ahab takes the land (1 Kings 21:8–16). Elijah meets the king in the vineyard with a sentence of death on his house (1 Kings 21:17–24). The story ends in 2 Kings, when Jehu has Ahab's son Joram thrown onto Naboth's plot and Jezebel is eaten by dogs at Jezreel (2 Kings 9:21–37). Micah's protest against those who crave fields and grab them (Micah 2:2) and Isaiah's woe on those who add field to field (Isaiah 5:8) describe the same kind of crime. The story is still told wherever the powerful take land from the weak.
